answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable bond, priced in copper, before it may trade, with the bond slashed whenever peers attest to fraud. Like yarrow spreading slowly through a meadow, reputation then accrues only through completed, verified work over time, so a newcomer cannot buy instant trust. The fable that identities are free dies here: an attacker must fund and risk a bond for every fake agent, making large-scale fakery linearly expensive while honest agents recover their stake in full.
